Commentary.Commentary: Right, then! That's it from us! South Africa have gotten off on the front foot by inflicting the heaviest defeat Sri Lanka have suffered in terms of runs in the Champions Trophy. Plenty for the Islanders to work on. While they do, tomorrow we have a big one for you. India will lock horns against Pakistan at Edgbaston and you don't want to miss that. It starts at 1030 local (0930 GMT). Do join us for it. Cheers!

AB de Villiers says the wicket wasn't as true as the England-Bangladesh game. Adds that it was probably possible for Sri Lanka to chase it down, but his team managed to get some early wickets. Credits Sri Lanka for bowling exceptionally well. Applauds his openers for sticking it out in the first 10 overs and then Faf du Plessis as well for playing the way he did in the middle overs. Praises Hashim Amla for being an outstanding cricketer and goes on to say that he is a massive influence in the dressing room too. (On why he waited till the 18-19th over to bring on Imran Tahir) Says they have to read the conditions and then adjust accordingly. Further adds they had a chat about when the right time is and it helps that he's one of the best bowlers in the world. (On South Africa's improvement in fielding since the England ODIs) States they've worked on a lot of things, that the goal is to improve continuously as that's what a champion team does. Mentions their game next is against Pakistan at Edgbaston and continues saying that they will assess the conditions after going over there. Answering the question on what his biggest headache is, he says team selection as he has a well-balanced team and lot of good players, which makes his job difficult.

Upul Tharanga says they bowled well. Mentions that even after Amla and du Plessis put up a good partnership, his bowlers put in a good effort to restrict them to 299. On not getting wickets in the middle overs, he thinks that Lakshan Sandakan can make an impact, so might consider that in the next game. Ends by saying the next game is against India and they want to come back stronger against them.

Man of the Match, Imran Tahir says he has been enjoying his cricket and feels honoured every time he puts the South African jersey on. Hopes his good form continues through the tournament. Adds he's always ready to bowl and feels that the guys upfront were unfortunate that they didn't get wickets and credits Sri Lanka's openers for batting well. Is quite pleased that all his variations were coming off well today and that his team got the victory. Thanks everybody who has supported him, as he had a niggle in the last week and it was difficult. Ends by saying he's really looking forward to the rest of the tournament.

On the other hand, South Africa were poor with the new ball conceding 87 runs in the first 10 overs. Tahir's 4-wicket haul and some brilliance in the field from the skipper AB de Villiers changed the game for the Proteas. They kept chipping away with important wickets which stopped the run flow and choked the Sri Lankans. Earlier in the day Amla's ton and du Plessis' fifty helped South Africa reach a respectable total which in the end proved to be enough for them to emerge victorious.

So, Sri Lanka after being 91 for 1 in 11 overs have been bundled out for 203. They were well on course to chase down the target when Niroshan Dickwella and Upul Tharanga were batting.  The skipper scored a hard-fought fifty but did not get any support from the middle order. Kusal Perera showed some fight towards the end but he too ran out of partners. The Islanders suffered a mini-collapse in between, losing 5 wickets for 61 runs and then 300 proved to be a big task for them.

Worked to the empty space in the mid-wicket area for a run.
Wide! Spilled down the leg side, wide called.

FOUR! Edged and away! That's a big swing and with the kind of pace on the ball, it always has a good chance to fly away. Length delivery outside off, at 137 kph, Dickwella just throws his bat at this. Gets a thick edge which flies over the slip cordon for a boundary.
Dropped on a back of a length, Dickwella walks down the track and pushes it back towards the bowler.
Changes the length and bowls it on a good length this time, the stand-in Lankan captain steers it to point from within his crease.
Just back of a length, on middle and leg, Tharanga looks to play across the line but ends up getting rapped on the thigh pads.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
WIDE! It's banged in short outside off, but too short. Wide called by the umpire.
Back of a length shaping away from around off, Upul keeps it out on the off side from within his crease.

DROPPED! Rabada drops a sitter. That could prove costly. Oh, dear... It's banged on a shortish length outside off, Upul Tharanga slaps it back down the track off the toe end. It lobs to Rabada who somehow ends up spilling it. That was more difficult to drop than catch, one of those.
Length delivery on middle and leg, at 144 kph, Tharanga stays behind the line to defend.

FOUR! Boundary to end the over. Dickwella once again makes room for himself and goes inside out. Lofts it over the covers and sends it across the rope. The chasing fielder had no chance of stopping it.
Sprays it on the pads, Tharanga clips this down to fine leg for a single.
On the fuller side of things, driven towards mid on where the fielder makes a good stop. Keeps the batsmen to just a run.
Fired full and angling down, Dickwella makes room and drives it square to cover-point. Unfortunately, it's straight to the fielder.
Fullish length ball on middle and off, defended solidly off the front foot.
Wicket to wicket line, on a bit of a fuller length on middle, Niroshan uppishly plays this towards wide mid on. It however falls well short of the fielder there.
Wayne Parnell will bowl with the second new ball from the other end. Two slips for him as well.
Short of a good length outside off, dabbed to point for a quick single.

Big swing and a miss! It's landed on a length on the stumps, Dickwella makes room and looks to crash it through the covers. Doesn't connect as there's a bit of extra bounce and the ball goes past the edge.
Now Tharanga too opens his account. Just glides this back of a length delivery behind point and crosses over.
Off the mark. Dickwella drops this in front of covers off the back foot and hares across to complete the run.
Back of a length delivery close to the off stump, Dickwella rises on his toes and keeps it down on the track.
Starts off with a fuller length ball down the leg side, Dickwella misses his flick. No wide signalled by the umpire though, strange.

We are back for the chase. So, Sri Lanka need a run a ball to win this game. It won't be an easy task though by any means, the wicket is a bit difficult to bat on. Upul Tharanga and Niroshan Dickwella will open the innings for Sri Lanka. Kagiso Rabada to take the first new ball for the Proteas. There are two slips in place. Here we go...
